summary: Trinidad and Tobago lets citizens of the 42 countries and territories on the Immigration Division’s no-visa list (among them the UK, Canada and most Commonwealth countries) enter without a visa, EU citizens (except Ireland) for up to 90 days in any 180 under the EU waiver agreement, and South Koreans for 90 days under a bilateral agreement; CARICOM nationals get six months under Caribbean free movement. US, Japanese, Brazilian, Irish, Turkish, Serbian and Colombian citizens are visa-free on their own governments’ official word, though the no-visa list does not name them. Most other nationalities must obtain a visa before traveling, online through the Immigration Division’s eVisa portal, which replaced all earlier visa procedures in April 2024.

vaccinations.text: Not an entry requirement: Trinidad and Tobago reports no yellow fever certificate requirement to WHO. Vaccination is recommended from 9 months of age for travellers going to densely forested areas of Trinidad, but not for itineraries limited to Tobago. notes: The UK government's travel advice says it is an offence for anyone, including children, to wear camouflage clothing or bring any into the country.

The UK government's travel advice says there are strict rules about goods you can take into or out of Trinidad and Tobago, and that you must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty.

payments.text: Tobago's official visitor site says Visa and Mastercard credit cards are widely accepted at businesses and ATMs, and that foreign currency can be changed at local banks. The UK government's travel advice says to use well-lit ATMs, withdraw small amounts and preferably do so in daylight.

safety.text: Trinidad has a high violent crime rate concentrated in specific areas of Port of Spain and the east-west corridor; several Western governments advise extra caution and the government has used states of emergency in recent years. Tourists are rarely targeted, but avoid walking at night, do not display valuables, and use pre-booked or hotel taxis rather than flagging cars. Tobago is markedly quieter, though break-ins to villas and rental cars occur.

The UK government's travel advice reports a high level of violent crime and advises particular caution in downtown Port of Spain, Carenage, Sea Lots, Belmont, Laventille, Morvant, Beetham, Barataria, Cocorite and the interior of Queens Park Savannah. It advises against walking at night, walking alone or using deserted beaches, and recommends well-established taxi firms recommended by locals or your hotel.

The officer decides how many days to grant on arrival. Check the stamp before you leave the hall. To stay longer, apply for an extension of time to remain at the Immigration Division in Port of Spain well before the stamp expires.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Trinidad and Tobago?
faq.answer: It depends on your passport. Citizens of the 42 countries and territories on the Immigration Division’s no-visa list — including the UK, Canada and most Commonwealth countries — need no visa, and neither do EU citizens (Ireland is outside the agreement), who get up to 90 days in any 180 under the EU waiver agreement, or South Koreans, who get 90 days under a bilateral agreement. US, Japanese, Brazilian, Irish, Turkish, Serbian and Colombian citizens are visa-free according to their own governments (and, for Brazil, Trinidad and Tobago’s embassy), although the no-visa list does not name them. CARICOM nationals enter under Caribbean free movement with up to six months. Everyone else — including Australian and most Latin American citizens, and Venezuelan passport holders — must obtain a visa before traveling, online through the Immigration Division’s eVisa portal, which replaced all earlier visa procedures in April 2024. Some foreign governments still tell their citizens no visa is needed; the Immigration Division's list is the authority.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Trinidad and Tobago without a visa?
faq.answer: It depends on your passport. EU citizens may stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period under the EU waiver agreement and South Koreans up to 90 days under a bilateral agreement; the British, Canadian, US and Japanese governments and Trinidad and Tobago’s embassy in Brazil also give 90 days, and Türkiye and Serbia 30. The Immigration Division’s no-visa list states no length of stay. In every case the immigration officer sets the period on arrival, so check your stamp, and apply to the Immigration Division for an extension of time to remain before it expires.

faq.question: What applies to CARICOM citizens?
faq.answer: Under the Revised Treaty of Chaguaramas, CARICOM nationals arriving as visitors are entitled to a definite entry of up to six months provided they have no adverse immigration record and can support themselves. Skilled nationals with a CARICOM Skills Certificate can additionally live and work in the country.

faq.question: Can Venezuelan citizens travel to Trinidad and Tobago visa-free?
faq.answer: No. Trinidad and Tobago ended visa-free entry for Venezuelan nationals and a visa must now be obtained in advance through the eVisa portal. Given the small sea crossing between the two countries, immigration enforcement on this route is strict — do not travel on an informal boat and confirm current rules with the Immigration Division before booking.

faq.question: Do I need anything special to attend Carnival?
faq.answer: No official source we could read describes a separate permit or visa for Carnival; visitors enter under the normal rules for their passport. The UK government's travel advice warns that robberies and opportunistic crime may occur during the Carnival period.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccination?
faq.answer: Not for entry: Trinidad and Tobago reports no yellow fever certificate requirement to WHO, whichever country you arrive from. Vaccination is recommended from 9 months of age if you are going to the densely forested areas of Trinidad, but not for trips limited to Tobago, and other countries may ask for a certificate when you arrive from Trinidad. Check before onward travel.
